Geovany Quenda 24. Reece James 25. Moises Caicedo 27. Malo Gusto 28. Teddy Sharman-Lowe 29. Pep Chavarria 30. Aaron Anselmino 31. Reggie Watson 32. Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli 33. Mykhailo Mudryk 34. Josh Acheampong 37. Tayo Subuloye 38. Tosin Adarabioyo 39. Mike Penders 41. Estevao 44. Gaga Slonina 45. Romeo Lavia

Mykailo Mudryk has also received a new number after being cleared to return to action following the resolution of his doping case.

The winger will wear the No.33 shirt this season, with his old No.10 now held by Cole Palmer.

Defender Tosin Adarabioyo no longer holds the No.4 jersey and instead has No.38, which was previously held by Guiu, who now doesn't have a number.

Chelsea begin their season away to local rivals Fulham on Monday night.

The two sides meet at Craven Cottage, with kick-off at 8pm live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish officially gets new Man City squad number after losing No.10 jersey
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish officially gets new Man City squad number after losing No.10 jersey

Jack Grealish has officially been given the No.18 shirt at Manchester City, in another hint he could be set to stay.

The forward made his first appearance for the Citizens in 453 days last weekend, as he was introduced at half time in their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal.



4 Grealish wore the No.18 in his first Man City appearance since May 2025 in the Community Shield Credit: Getty

After the match, new City boss Enzo Maresca appeared to suggest Grealish could yet have a future at the Etihad Stadium.

This comes after the England international spent last season on loan at Everton, before the Toffees opted against triggering their option to buy clause.

New beginning for Grealish?

While speculation continues over where Grealish could end up next, he remains a City player for the time being.



And the club appear to have taken steps to confirm this following his Sky Blues return in the Community Shield.

After coming on at half time in the 3-0 defeat, the 30-year-old wore the No.18 shirt in a new sight to fans.



Grealish had donned the No.10 during his City career up until his loan to Everton last season, when he lost it to Rayan Cherki.

And now the Englishman is back in Manchester, it appears he has been forced into a permanent number change.



After wearing it on his back during the Community Shield, the winger will officially wear the No.18 on his shirt this term.

Man City have confirmed this on their website, with Grealish previously appearing on their squad list without a number.

Now though, he is credited with his new number, which previously belonged to recently-departed goalkeeper Stefan Ortega.

4 Grealish was given the No.10 shirt at Man City upon arrival for a then-British record £100million fee in 2021 Credit: AFP



4 Cherki was then handed the maverick number last summer before Grealish joined Everton on loan Credit: Getty

While Ortega last donned the No.18 at the club, Fabian Delph, Frank Lampard and Gareth Barry have all also worn the digits before.

Coincidentally, Grealish wore the same number at Everton last season, though it is unclear whether it carries any sentimental value.

What is the latest on Jack Grealish?

Grealish's change in shirt number comes just days after Man City boss Maresca hinted he could feature for the side this season.



Speaking after the Community Shield, Maresca explained: "He's here with us. Until he's not here with us I'll try to help him.

"If he's here he will play games."

Grealish joined City in a £100million deal from Aston Villa back in 2021.

4 Enzo Maresca has refused to rule out a future for Grealish at the Etihad Credit: AFP

Having signed a six-year contract, his deal does not expire until the end of the season.



This has led to huge speculation he would leave the Etihad this summer, even after Everton opted not to take up the £50m buy option in his loan deal.

Their decision came after he registered one goal and six assists in 22 appearances for the Toffees, having missed the end of last season as he underwent surgery on a foot fracture in February.

talkSPORT previously reported Grealish was drawing interest from Saudi side Al Hilal, while he sent the rumour mill into overdrive when he was spotted at Wrexham's Championship opener against Cardiff on Monday.

The playmaker has made 158 appearances for Man City in all competitions, scoring 17 goals and providing 23 assists.



He has won seven major trophies including three Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Sports.title: Man City line up Enzo Fernandez bid five days after missing Chelsea deadline
Sports.content:
Man City line up Enzo Fernandez bid five days after missing Chelsea deadline

Manchester City intend to bid for Enzo Fernandez, talkSPORT understands.

It comes despite Enzo Maresca's side missing the 5pm deadline on Friday set by Chelsea for offers to be made.

5 City intend to bid for Fernandez despite missing Chelsea's self-imposed deadline Credit: Getty

City sources believe the Blues are open to a sale despite their self-imposed cut-off point to place a £120million bid passing.

Chelsea are currently working on the premise that Fernandez will remain at the club beyond the end of the transfer window.

The midfielder has been training as usual this week ahead of their Premier League opener against Fulham on Monday.

However, those close to the 2022 World Cup winner say Fernandez is open to a move to the Etihad Stadium.

His preference had previously been to join Real Madrid this summer, only for the Spanish side to issue a statement revealing they did not plan to launch a bid.

It is understood that Chelsea received no offers for the 25-year-old from any potential suitors before their deadline passed.

talkSPORT also understands Roma star Manu Kone is also on City's list of midfield targets.

What has Enzo Maresca said about Enzo Fernandez?

While a deal appeared to be dead in the water after City failed to meet their deadline, Maresca's comments hours earlier suggest there could yet be another twist.

Speaking ahead of his side's Community Shield clash with Arsenal on Sunday, the Italian appeared unfazed about Fernandez.

Maresca admitted on midday on Friday that City would not be making a move for the Chelsea star before 5pm that evening.

5 Maresca appeared laid back about City's pursuit of Fernandez Credit: Getty

5 The Argentine recently returned to Chelsea training following his World Cup exploits Credit: Getty

Asked about the cut-off point, Maresca said: "I don't think we're going to do something today."

The City boss also said of Fernandez: "He is a player from another club.

"I don't think it's correct to talk about other players. I'm not going to say anything about players who are not with us."

Having only ruled out any business for Fernandez on Friday, Maresca appeared to suggest that City would make further additions this summer, pointing out they have until transfer deadline day on September 1.

He added: “When the window is open, we can buy players and we can sell players.

“For sure there are things that we need to do, can be one can be two [new signings], it depends if they want to leave.”

5 Maresca and Fernandez shared a close bond while at Chelsea Credit: Getty

Could Chelsea be playing a 'game of poker?'

With Maresca remaining coy on City's interest in Fernandez, talkSPORT's Alex Crook and Gabby Agbonlahor both questioned if Chelsea will hold firm on their stance.

Crook suggested Maresca could be deliberately looking to test his former club's resolve, having left Stamford Bridge in January after a breakdown in relations at the club.

Speaking on Friday's talkSPORT, Crook said: “It's a game of poker, isn't it? Enzo Maresca's playing the game there. I'm sure he delivered it with a glint in his eye.

“I'm suspicious of this hard deadline. That's the information we're getting out of Chelsea.

“If the £120m offer is not made in written format today by 5pm, then Enzo Fernandez won't be going anywhere this summer.”

Agbonlahor also questioned Chelsea's ultimatum over Fernandez, insisting City are well within their rights to try and sign him anytime before the transfer window closes.

5 City need new bodies in midfield after Rodri's departure to Barcelona Credit: Getty

He chimed in: “I don't like the fact that you're giving them an ultimatum today when there's still over two weeks left of the transfer window.

“If I'm Manchester City, we'll do it in our own time.”

A move for Fernandez was believed to hinge on Rodri leaving City to join Barcelona.

LaLiga giants Barca have completed the £65.3million signing of the Ballon d'Or winner.

Fernandez is among the Cityzens' potential replacements and now faces an uncertain future in west London, after he previously fuelled rumours of his exit.

The Blues midfielder heavily hinted at a move to Real Madrid towards the end of last season, only for the Spanish giants to shut this down in a statement saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

While Man City have an interest in Fernandez, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs recently suggested his £120m asking price could be an obstacle.

The Cityzens have so far signed Elliot Anderson for £116m, while they are now in advanced talks with Lille over Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, for a fee expected to be in the region of £100m.

Jacobs claimed this could leave City reluctant to make another nine-digit transfer this summer.

Sports.title: Ederson makes first public comments about failed Manchester United transfer
Sports.content:
Ederson says he 'doesn't know' why his move to Manchester United fell through earlier this summer.

The Brazil midfielder had looked set to join the Red Devils from Atalanta after the World Cup with United agreeing a deal worth around £39million with the Serie A club prior to the tournament.

4 Ederson admits he 'doesn't know' why his move to United fell through earlier this summer Credit: Getty

A medical then took place once Brazil were knocked out in the last 16 stage.

However, the deal had collapsed after an issue was flagged during Ederson's medical and United opted not to proceed with the signing.

Atalanta maintained that the 27-year-old was fully fit, though, before handing Ederson a new five-year deal.

His previous contract had been due to expire next summer, prompting United to launch their initial move.

Ederson on failed United move

Ederson has now spoken publicly for the first time on the failed transfer as he prepares to return to competitive action with Atalanta.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, he admitted: "I honestly don’t know what happened.

"I always had interest from other clubs, and I could’ve gone to another English side.

"The tests went well, I don’t know what changed. I’ve been with Atalanta for four years and always played.

"I could’ve just waited to see what happened, but the great rapport with the club convinced me to stay and sign a new contract."

He also spoke to reporters during a press conference prior to Atalanta's Conference League play-off tie against Hapoel Tel Aviv.

4 United pulled out of a deal for the Atalanta midfielder following his medical Credit: Getty

Revealing the factos behind his decision to commit his future to the club, he said: "I am very happy to remain with Atalanta, I really thank the club and Luca Percassi (Atalanta CEO).

"They called me many times, I felt they were by my side, but even though I had interest from other clubs, after everything that happened, I thought it was best to stick with who really wanted me, and that was always Atalanta.

"I was happy to wear the jersey that has given me so much joy."

As for the impact of the transfer saga, he added: "I had lovely moments going to the World Cup with Brazil, and then I still don’t know what happened to be honest, but the important thing is that I was able to deal with the situation, return with the right mentality and give my all to the club that gave me so much.

"I am still Ederson, everyone knows me here and what I can do, they know I will always give my all."

Ederson joined Atalanta from Italian club Salernitana back in 2022 and has since scored 16 goals and added six assists in 180 appearances.

4 Ederson has since signed a new five-year deal after returning to Atalanta following the World Cup Credit: Getty

United's midfield overhaul

Despite missing out on Ederson, Michael Carrick has already brought in two new midfielders this summer, following the departure of Casemiro to Inter Miami on a free transfer.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have since moved to Old Trafford from Chelsea and Aston Villa, respectively.

Meanwhile, Carlos Baleba could soon become United's fourth signing of the summer.

talkSPORT understands the Brighton midfielder has already agreed personal terms over a move to the Red Devils.

United are now in advanced talks with the Seagulls after lodging a bid worth an initial £60million plus a further £5million in add-ons.

Sports.title: Tottenham in talks to sign Savinho and Omar Marmoush as Man City’s asking price for pair revealed
Sports.content:
Tottenham in talks to sign Savinho and Omar Marmoush as Man City’s asking price for pair revealed

Tottenham Hotspur are attempting to sign Manchester City duo Savinho and Omar Marmoush, talkSPORT understands.

Roberto De Zerbi's side are in talks with their Premier League rivals over the attacking pair.



3 Spurs are in talks with City over a double deal for Savinho and Marmoush Credit: Getty

Although any potential deal is yet to be finalised, discussions between the clubs are advancing with City prepared to sanction move for both players if the north London side are prepared to stump up around £150million.

It comes after Savinho was left out of the matchday squad for City's Community Shield defeat to Arsenal on Sunday.

Marmoush did make a cameo appearance during the second half, though, as his side fell to a 3-0 defeat.



talkSPORT revealed last month that Savinho had informed City of his desire to join Spurs after their previous interest a year ago.

Talks over the winger have been ongoing since the early stages of the summer transfer window.



Savinho signed a new deal at the Etihad Stadium in October through to the summer of 2031.

Meanwhile, Marmoush was signed from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025 on a four-and-a-half-year contract.



The Egypt forward has since scored 16 goals in 62 appearances for City across all competitions.

Spurs transfer plans

Spurs' interest in Savinho and Marmoush comes as City look to fund their own midfield revamp.

Enzo Maresca's side are seeking sales as they pursue potential deals for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez.

3 Savinho informed City of his desire to join Spurs earlier this summer Credit: Getty



Cody Gakpo also remains a target for Spurs, who would prefer to sign all three of their current prospective additions.

However, the Netherlands man is currently the toughest of the trio to negotiate unless Liverpool sign a new attacker of their own.

Spurs have already spent over £200million this summer on deals for Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi have also joined the club on free transfers ahead of the new season.



talkSPORT verdict

Spurs' move for Marmoush comes after they were urged to bolster their goal threat with a new striker.

Speaking on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Spurs, Sonny Snelling explained: "I've been quite harsh on Richarlison. I compared him to a shovel about this time last year.

3 Spurs ideally want to sign Gakpo in addition to Savinho and Marmoush Credit: Getty

"I don't think he's the perfect striker for what De Zerbi wants. I think that is Solanke. I think Solanke would be the perfect striker, but he can't stay fit. Another injury picked up in pre-season.



"If we sign Gakpo, I think he comes into the club as probably our best finisher. I really do and that sums up our front line.

"The fact that you're not getting too many goals from the players who are already there. I think Mohammed Kudus is due for a good season when he's back from injury as well.

"But to me, the way that goals are probably going to be spread around this team you don't necessarily need a player who's going to get 20, 25, 30.

"I don't think we've got the finances to really go out and sign an [Victor] Osimhen on wages like that.



"So if you get in a player and him and Richarlison, or whoever, can fight out for that starting spot and they get 10 goals each or 15 then you're in a good place there.

"That's why I've seen a lot of people sort of warm to the idea of Nicolas Jackson because he does get a goal return.

"He can be quite wasteful, but the amount of chances we're going to get, it will hopefully finish a few. So maybe that is a viable option."

Sports.title: Frank Lampard suffers major blow as key Coventry player out for up to three months
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard suffers major blow as key Coventry player out for up to three months

Coventry City will be without promotion-winning star Haji Wright for their Premier League return.

Manager Frank Lampard confirmed the USA striker could be sidelined for as long as three months with a 'very serious quad injury'.



2 Wright was included in the USA's World Cup squad after impressing in Coventry's promotion-winning campaign Credit: Getty

Coventry lose a major source of goals

Wright enjoyed the best scoring season of his Coventry career last term, helping fire the Sky Blues to the Championship title with 17 goals.

The 28-year-old has found the net 49 times in all competitions since arriving from Turkish club Antalyaspor three years ago, becoming the Sky Blues' record signing at the time.

He was one of four Coventry players named in the 2025/26 Championship Team of the Season.



Wright will have been looking forward to his first taste of the Premier League but missed his side's final two pre-season friendlies against Espanyol and Monaco.

And he won't be involved when the Sky Blues kick off the new campaign away to champions Arsenal on Friday night, live on talkSPORT.



Wright's injury 'disappointing for everyone'

Speaking in the build-up that clash, Coventry's first Premier League match for 25 years, Lampard confirmed: "Haji Wright won’t be available for the Arsenal game.

"He won’t be available for a little while; he’s got a very serious quad injury which is disappointing for Haji and for us.



"It’s certainly going to be a number of weeks – could even be up to 12 weeks."

While Wright's absence comes as a big blow, Lampard isn't short of attacking options after a busy summer of transfer activity.

Coventry have signed two strikers this week alone, completing deals to bring in Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest and Sidiki Cherif from Fenerbahce.

2 Awoniyi adds valuable Premier League experience from his time at Forest Credit: Getty



The Sky Blues have broken their transfer record a whopping four times this window, with Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi their most expensive new acquisition from Danish side Nordsjaelland at £23.1m.

Coventry to do even more business?

And Lampard hasn't ruled out further signings before deadline day on August 31.

"We will see," he said. "We knew we had work to do and we knew what the gap [between the Championship and the Premier League] is because history tells you that.

"We've tried to strike the balance of working smartly in the window to bring in players to help the squad we already had. We will see for the remainder of the window about ins and outs."



Looking ahead to the game, Lampard said: "I want to show in our performance and how we approach the game that we're not coming into it with fear.

"We respect Arsenal greatly, but it doesn't mean you play with too much respect that you are passive. We can hopefully show we are a good team that want to do something this year."

Coventry's primary goal for 2026/27 will be preserving their Premier League status, and they've been tipped to stay up by talkSPORT Breakfast presenter Jeff Stelling and regular talkSPORT guest Darragh MacAnthony, chairman of Peterborough United.

The Sky Blues previously spent 34 years in the top flight from their promotion to the old First Division in 1967 to their relegation from the Premier League in 2001.

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s ideal Morgan Rogers replacement named amid Manchester United and Tottenham interest
Sports.content:
How does one go about replacing the most expensive British footballer in history?

Well, that's a problem Aston Villa boss Unai Emery must solve ahead of the 2026/27 campaign following Morgan Rogers' £117million exit to Chelsea earlier this summer.

4 Rogers helped end Villa's 30-year wait for a trophy Credit: Getty

The eye-watering nine-figure fee represents a significant profit on the initial £8m Villa forked out to sign Rogers from Middlesbrough in January 2024.

After a six-month period of adjustment, Rogers quickly cemented himself as one of Villa's most important players.

His brilliance in the final third was reflected by his 56 goal contributions across all competitions in the last two seasons, split evenly with 28 goals and 28 assists.

But Rogers' departure now leaves a gaping hole in Villa's line-up and it's one that won't be fixed on the cheap.

The reigning Europa League champions have already taken a step in the right direction by snapping up Johan Manzambi from Freiburg in a club record deal.

However, Manzambi's Villa debut may be some way away as he continues to recover from a knee injury sustained while representing Switzerland at the World Cup, with no definitive return date provided.

Andy Brassell reveals who Aston Villa should sign to fill Morgan Rogers void

While the 20-year-old recovers, Villa could still add extra strength to their attacking midfield stocks.

And according to European football expert Andy Brassell, Villa may find that in Como ace Martin Baturina.

"I think he makes a lot of sense for Aston Villa in a post-Morgan Rogers world," Brassell told talkSPORT.com.

"And he's a different player to Rogers of course. And you would expect Baturina ultimately to score more goals than him. So I feel that would work quite well.

4 Baturina has quickly become a talent to watch after his first season with Como Credit: Getty

"In terms of the blend that Manchester United are trying to put together. Yes I think he'd be a plus for them.

"But again, for me, Villa seems a really really good fit."

Is there another English team Martin Baturina could play for?

Another English team Brassell mentioned as a potential suitor for Baturina was Tottenham Hotspur.

However, Spurs already boast multiple players in Baturina's mould, which Brassell describes as 'more of a second striker' and 'someone who relies on excellent close control' in the box.

"And what they (Spurs) could do with is a big, brutish centre forward, essentially," Brassell continued.

"Look, I know De Zerbi wants to play fluid football. So maybe it does stack up. Maybe it could work.

4 Emery is in need of refreshing his attack following Rogers' move to Chelsea Credit: Getty

"But it wouldn't be my first choice destination for him."

How did Martin Baturina perform last season for Como?

Baturina, who joined Como from Dinamo Zagreb last summer, ended the 2025/26 campaign with eight goals and four assists across all competitions.

The 23-year-old boosted his transfer value with a goal during Croatia's 4-2 loss to England at the World Cup.

That can only be good news for Como, who are already one of Serie A's wealthiest clubs.

But that hasn't stopped club president Mirwan Suwarso from leaving the door open for a potential summer exit.

"If there's an offer, we'll listen," Suwarso told Calciomercato.

4 The 23-year-old helped Como qualify for the Champions League Credit: Getty

"If we like it, we'll accept it, but we're not afraid to refuse."

Why Martin Baturina will not be cheap for interested clubs

Suwarso's hard line stance is not ideal for Villa and other potential suitors, who almost certainly won't be able to strike a cut-price deal.

"There are two ways to look at it," Brassell told talkSPORT.com.

"Firstly, the fact is they're very well backed. A lot better backed than a lot of the traditional big names in Italian football. So to try and force them into a sale is quite difficult.

"As you said, if they're going to sell, they’ll sell on their terms.

"Baturina was really, really good last season. And bear in mind that as we spoke about before, that Alvaro Morata gap in terms of goals.

"They were short because he wasn't putting the ball in the back of the net. So they needed other people to chip in. Baturina was able to do that."

Sports.title: Man City urged to snub Enzo Fernandez and sign £60million Premier League alternative
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been told to consider signing Adam Wharton instead of Enzo Fernandez as they look to replace Rodri.

The Citizens are looking to add another midfielder to their ranks after influential midfielder Rodri left to join Barcelona for a fee in the region of £65million.

4 Rodri's departure to Barcelona has now been confirmed, after he previously looked set to join Real Madrid Credit: Getty

While the departure of Spain's World Cup-winning captain is a huge loss, City appear to have made replacing him a priority this summer.

Elliot Anderson was signed for £116m at the start of the window, and Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi is also expected to move to the Etihad, with personal terms agreed with Lille.

However, after Rodri's exit, another star is likely to be needed to bolster their midfield options.

Chelsea's Fernandez has been heavily linked with a move, although any deal is currently up in the air after the Citizens missed his 5pm deadline last Friday to complete their business.

Wharton tipped for big move

With Chelsea demanding £120m for Fernandez, City would once again have to complete a nine-digit transfer to snap up the Argentina star.

But talkSPORT's McCoist felt there is a better option available, and one which is likely to prove less expensive.

He pointed to Crystal Palace star Wharton, who has long been tipped for a big move, with Manchester United's interest already known.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, McCoist said: “I like him [Wharton] a lot…

"I think Wharton is more like Rodri than Fernandez is, I don’t think they’re going to get like-for-like now Rodri’s left, he’s the best at what he does.

“But I think you’d make a case that Wharton [is more like Rodri].

4 Wharton continues to be linked with England's biggest clubs Credit: Getty

4 Enzo Fernandez faces an uncertain future at Chelsea Credit: Getty

“The ball comes to him and the first thing he does is look forward, I really like him, I think he’d be an excellent signing.”

With Wharton earning huge praise for his ability to dictate play in midfield, this makes him more similar in profile to Rodri.

Palace’s price tag for him is unclear, although it was previously reported that Man United were plotting a £60m bid this summer.

That now appears unlikely to materialise, but if the Eagles demand a fee in this region, it would make Wharton a far cheaper option than Fernandez.

The 22-year-old has impressed since his move to Selhurst Park in February 2024, with his technical ability and vision catching the eye.

His exploits saw him named in England Euro 2024 squad, but he was a notable omission by Thomas Tuchel for this summer's World Cup.

4 A move to Man City would likely boost Wharton's England career, who has earned four senior caps to date Credit: Getty

Despite this, Wharton has continued to draw admirers, and his performance in Palace's Conference League final victory over Rayo Vallecano even saw him labelled good enough to play for Real Madrid or Bayern Munich.

The Blackburn academy graduate is poised to begin the new season at Palace, who are gearing up for Europa League football after Conference League glory.

There's also a new coach at the helm of Palace in Pierre Sage, who takes over from Oliver Glasner after he left at the end of his contract, but has since joined Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: England SAW BALL IN HALF so Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue can share it after both celebrating brilliant five-wicket hauls against Pakistan
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue found a novel way of celebrating the twin five-wicket hauls that decimated Pakistan at Headingley - taking half a match ball home each.

As they left the field shoulder to shoulder to the acclaim of the Leeds locals after Pakistan were dismissed for 171, they hatched a plan to share the leather sphere as a memento.

Producing his half from his pocket at the post-match press conference, Robinson revealed: ‘We were walking off and Tonguey said it. I told him it would actually be quite cool.’

Within five minutes of being back in the home dressing room, England team manager Wayne Bentley was dispatched to ask groundsman Richie Robinson to saw it in two.

‘You don’t have too many half cricket balls, so it will be something we never forget. It’s not too often that two guys get a five-for in the same innings. It’s a nice gesture.’

Josh Tongue (5-46) and Ollie Robinson (5-51) share the plaudits as they leave the field

... and Robinson late holds up his half of the sawn-off ball, with Tongue keeping the other!

It has been quite a week for Robinson, who welcomed daughter Eva to the world last Thursday and then marked his return to England colours at his former Yorkshire headquarters by taking a wicket with the first ball of the match.

Robinson, 32, marked his return from a two-year international exile with five first-innings wickets and the man-of-the-match award against New Zealand at Lord’s in June, but then missed the following two Tests due to injury at The Oval and on selection grounds at Trent Bridge.

But his fifth five-wicket bag in 22 appearances has England in control on Joe Root’s return to the Test captaincy.

England resume on day two with Root unbeaten on 37 in a score of 112 for two.

Sports.title: Now Man City turn to France midfielder Manu Kone - a target for rivals United this summer - as their post-Pep revolution gathers pace
Sports.content:
Now Man City turn to France midfielder Manu Kone - a target for rivals United this summer - as their post-Pep revolution gathers pace

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City have identified Roma’s Manu Kone as a potential signing for their revamped midfield after selling Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders.

Both midfielders departed this week for a combined total of around £110million, leaving Enzo Maresca with holes to fill in his squad just days before the Premier League season starts.

City are hopeful of wrapping up a deal for Lille’s deep-lying midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, valued at £85m, in the coming days to bolster that area of the pitch.

And Daily Mail Sport understands that Kone – who featured five times for France during the World Cup – is on the list of those to target before the window closes.

The 25-year-old has spent the past two years in Serie A, scoring four goals in 63 appearances for Roma, but is more renowned for his dynamism and excels off the ball.

Roma are reported to have set an asking price of around £51m for Kone – a broadly similar figure to that paid by Al-Qadsiah for Reijnders.

Both Chelsea and Manchester United have been linked with the former Borussia Monchengladbach man. Daily Mail Sport last month revealed how United had spoken to his representatives, but they are now swooping for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba.

Roma midfielder Manu Kone featured five times for France during the World Cup and is now on Manchester City's list of targets for the summer

Kone, who has 19 caps for France, started four of their matches in North America over the summer and came on at half time in their semi-final defeat by Spain.

City remain interested in Enzo Fernandez, with Chelsea’s soft deadline to complete a deal for £120m having passed without a formal bid. The Argentina midfielder wants to link back up with Maresca but City are unwilling to reach Chelsea’s demands.

In what promises to be a frantic final fortnight of the window, Newcastle are also exploring a move for Nico Gonzalez.

City are in advanced talks to sell both Savinho and Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

The two deals combined would likely be worth upwards of £140m, with Daily Mail Sport revealing earlier in the week that Spurs were pressing ahead with those moves.

Maresca recently suggested that both players were considering their futures after a lack of minutes last term.

Sports.title: The day English cricket desperately needed: Joe Root enjoys perfect return to Test captaincy as England dominate Pakistan after Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue show match-winning credentials, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
If Joe Root could have scripted the perfect start to his full-time return to the England captaincy, it might have looked something like this.

Tougher tasks lie ahead than bowling first under glowering northern skies against a Pakistan batting line-up devoid of form and confidence, but this was a day English cricket desperately needed after the chaos that has engulfed it.

Ollie Robinson settled nerves by taking a wicket with the first ball of this three-match series, an unprecedented moment in a Test in this country. Later, both he and Josh Tongue each celebrated a five-for in a total of 171 – in successive balls, no less, one man’s class instantly backed up by the other’s.

Then, as if to suggest Root had other forces on his side too, the clouds parted just as Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay walked out to forge the reply.

Earlier, sweeping rain had triggered an early lunch, delaying the restart for two and a quarter hours. Now, the sun shone on England’s endeavours, drawing a little of the sting from the surface. At stumps, they had hurried to 112 for two at four and a half an over, with Root unbeaten and ominous on 37.

Not everything went according to plan. Jofra Archer looked devoid of rhythm after his white-ball exertions in the Hundred. Nor was Gus Atkinson at his best, only three days after appearing in the final at Lord’s for Manchester Super Giants.

Josh Tongue and Ollie Robinson both took five wickets as England dominated day one of the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley

Robinson bowled with skill and control to take his second five-for in two Tests this summer

Tongue bowled with pace and hostility and took four wickets in 11 balls either side of tea

But Tongue played in that game too, and it didn’t stop him taking four wickets in 11 balls either side of tea – the kind of rapid burst that confirmed a different talent from Robinson, who regularly operated below 80mph, striving for skill not speed.

And Robinson it was who had opened the door through which England happily barged, held up only by a third-wicket stand of 91 between Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique.

In June, he had marked his return to the Test side after an absence of two and a half years with a triple-wicket maiden against New Zealand at Lord’s and a career-best five for 39. But if that underlined his prowess, his subsequent knee injury, followed by England’s refusal to trust him in searing temperatures in Nottingham, resurrected old grumbles about his fitness.

It raised the prospect that England – certainly under Brendon McCullum – might pigeon-hole him as a grey-skies specialist. And when Root won the toss, Robinson could not have asked for more.

His first ball jagged back into the left-handed Azan Awais, bringing both his 500th first-class wicket and a roar from the Headingley crowd as umpire Chris Gaffaney gave his assent.

And Pakistan were six for two when Robinson, with his first ball from over the wicket to Shan Masood, another leftie, won an even more adjacent lbw appeal. It set the tone for a day on which nine of the 12 wickets were either leg-before or bowled – old-fashioned reward for pitching the ball up on a Headingley surface that was helpful but not extravagantly so.

Tongue chipped in when Imam edged low to Harry Brook at second slip for 42, before Robinson pinned Saud Shakeel for five, and was grateful when Shakeel’s request for a review came a fraction too late: DRS suggested the ball would have cleared leg stump.

When, with Jamie Smith up to the stumps, Robinson brought a beauty back through the gate to bowl Shafique for a hard-earned 61, Pakistan were 118 for five and on the downward slope.

Root admitted recently that he overbowled Archer during his first spell in charge. Now, he seemed in danger of doing the same to Robinson: of England’s first 40 overs, he had bowled 16, including a second spell of two for 17 off eight, an answer to the accusation that he needs the new ball to thrive.

Fortunately for Root, it didn’t matter that Archer had mislaid his radar, or that Atkinson lacked consistency. Tongue bowled Salman Agha, Pakistan’s stand-in captain, for 21, then speared a 91mph missile onto Ali Usman’s front pad, triggering tea at 150 for seven.

After the break, Khurram Shahzad hammered the hat-trick ball through the covers, but the end came quickly. Tongue won a marginal lbw shout against an aghast Mohammad Rizwan, before Robinson had Shahzad slogging to mid-on to complete his five-for. Next ball, Tongue joined him, knocking over Mohammad Abbas’s off stump.

England closed on 112-2 in response to Pakistan's 171 all out after Joe Root and Jordan Cox built a promising partnership

It was pretty much the perfect day for Joe Root as he returned to the England Test captaincy

Not since 2006, when Steve Harmison and Monty Panesar performed the feat against Pakistan at Old Trafford, had two England bowlers taken five wickets in the same Test innings, and Robinson cheerfully jostled for the match ball with Tongue as they led the team off the field.

Robinson’s comeback summer has now brought him 12 wickets at 10. If Root and – when he arrives – Stephen Fleming can turn him into a threat in all conditions, they will unlock the match-winner McCullum had hoped for before his patience snapped.

Pakistan’s swift decline – their last eight fell for 74 – left England two hours to bat.

Duckett narrowly survived an lbw appeal from Abbas third ball, which irritated the Pakistanis, but got only as far as 15 before Abbas won the day’s sixth leg-before verdict.

Gay, meanwhile, hit seven stylish fours before he was squared up by Mohammad Ali and caught at second slip for a 31-ball 33.

Agha brought Rizwan up to the stumps during a tireless 10-over spell from Abbas, but Jordan Cox, in his first Test innings at No 3, and Root – having been cheered to the middle by his fellow Yorkshiremen – were up to the task.

Sports.title: Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Wrexham aim high with look at Leeds star Lucas

Wrexham are showing interest in an ambitious move for Leeds United forward Lukas Nmecha.

The 27-year-old joined Leeds last summer from Wolfsburg and scored seven goals in 37 appearances.

The Welsh side are also exploring a deal for free agent centre-back and Congo international Axel Tuanzebe.

Spurs push on with Marmoush and Savinho swoops

Tottenham are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over the double deal of Savinho and Omar Marmoush.

As Daily Mail Sport previously revealed, Spurs have identified the Brazilian winger and Egyptian forward as two targets for their forward line along with Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

The deal with City would not be cheap, however, while coach Enzo Maresca also wants to ensure he has enough bodies with Jeremy Doku out for the start of the season.

Liverpool, meanwhile, need to ensure they strengthen their own attacking options before allowing anyone to leave and would want a considerable fee to even consider selling Gakpo. Tottenham have made their interest known.

Villa and Marseille keen on Chelsea's Tosin - after he loses No4 shirt

Aston Villa hold interest in Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo but face competition from Marseille.

Adarabioyo is one of a number of options being considered by Unai Emery.

The 6ft 5ins centre-back had been willing to stay at Stamford Bridge and fight for his place but it is becoming apparent it would be in his career's best interests to explore a move away where he would have a more prominent role.

Villa have been assessing names throughout the window after it became clear Arsenal would pursue Ezri Konsa who is likely to wrap up his £51m move to the champions by the weekend.

Adarabioyo also has other other clubs to consider.

Marseille have made contact with Chelsea and are deemed most likely to pursue a move as it stands.

Tosin Adarabioyo signs a shirt for a fan in Hong Kong on Chelsea's pre-season tour

Sevilla are also keen as are Marco Silva's Benfica but are not considered as strong as Marseille and Villa.

Other clubs are also now showing interest in the 28-year-old who joined as a free agent after leaving Fulham in 2024.

In another ominous sign, Adarabioyo has also lost his shirt number in a squad list reshuffle.

Formerly No 4, Adarabioyo will now wear No 38. New signing Valentin Barco takes his old shirt.

Liam Delap is no longer No 9 and will wear No 12,with Joao Pedro taking the No 9.

Chslsea bag Hearts' Osborne

Chelsea have signed 17-year-old centre-back Alfie Osborne from Hearts for £400,000.

Osborne captained Hearts’ U18s to the Scottish FA Youth Cup and has also captained Scotland's U19s.

Reijnders seals Saudi move

Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has joined Al Qadsiah for £52m.

Reijnders will work under Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah.

The 28-year-old, who has an offer from Nottingham Forest also, only joined City from AC Milan last summer for £46.3m and made 50 appearances, scoring seven goals.

Tijjani Reijnders is leaving Manchester City after just one season

Clarets land Coudet

Burnley have signed goalkeeper Gregoire Coudet from French side Brest on a permanent deal. The 27-year-old has signed a four-year contract.

Norwich City have signed Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan.

The Championship club will pay a proportion of the 25-year-old's salary after finding a replacement for Ali Ahmed following his knee injury.

Inter hopeful of £30m deal for Jones

Liverpool and Inter Milan have resumed talks over a deal for Curtis Jones today, initiated by the Italian side.

There is currently no agreement for the 25-year-old but terms are being discussed.

Something in line with the package and structure Inter utilised to sign Tottenham defender Djed Spence - €35m (£30m) - will likely see a deal agreed for the midfielder between the clubs.

However, club sources underline these are verbal negotiations at present, and no actual agreement has been reached.

Toffees consider Cash grab

Everton are showing interest in Aston Villa right back Matty Cash as they assess all options in the market.

Villa are signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham today and he is being brought in to increase competition for Cash in the right-back berth. Poland international Cash has three years left on contract.

Everton have been working through a raft of names to try and solve their issue at right-back which has even prompted questions from Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Barca keep tabs on Kane

Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich.

The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old.

Kane is understood to want a three year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known.

Read the full story here.

Villa braced for another Watkins bid

Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old.

Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia

The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki.

Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma.

Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa.

The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today.

The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million.

There's a new Cherif in town

Coventry have completed their ninth signing of the summer transfer window with Fenerbahce striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5million.

The deal has taken the club's spending to over £120m.

The 19-year-old, who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January, made appearances in the Europa League and in this season’s Champions League qualifiers prior to opening talks with Coventry.

Toon's Nkunku offer

Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan.

However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed.

Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others.

... and they're closing in on Diabate

Newcastle are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate.

The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest.

However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season.

Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far.

Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move

Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan.

The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out.

The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future.

First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany.

Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today.

Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely.

Konsa nearing Arsenal move...

Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa.

The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow.

Read the full story here.

As Gunners move for United youngster

Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United.

Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon.

Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season.

England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan.

Baleba close to United switch

Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared.

Read the full story here.

Pogba tears up Monaco deal

Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end.

The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS.

Read the full story here.

Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder

Farke reunites with Elvedi

Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses.

The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club.

James set for Wolves move

Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical.

The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m.

He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham.

Chelsea defender closes on Italy move

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning.

The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m.

Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal.

The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains.

The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull.

Piroe party at West Ham

West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season.

The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League.

Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds

West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons.

Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League.

'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.'

Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League.

The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Potters snare Ipswich pair

Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan.

Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses.

Sports.title: Reaping the rewards of trading funkiness for patience, paying a price for moving in the field... and working on getting the best from Jofra Archer: What we learned from Joe Root's first day back as England's Test captain
Sports.content:
Ahead of his second stint as England’s Test captain, Joe Root vowed to ‘evolve with the rhythm of the game.’

In contrast to the clunkiness that marred the back end of his initial five-year tenure, the moves made in response to events unfolding amid the home comforts of Headingley took on a much more natural feel.

Root’s first call was to ask Pakistan to bat at a venue unique for its dramatic mood swings. Look up not down, they say, when making such decisions, because if the sun is out, the pitch becomes exceedingly flat, as it did when England chased 371 to beat India on the final day here last year.

However, under cloud cover, the ball can hoop round corners. And this, as the man himself acknowledged by referencing ‘the overhead conditions and moisture under the surface’ was a bowling day.

With three new-ball operators in England’s XI, there was also an early decision to make on who would get choice of ends - and indeed who would be held back until first change.

Joe Root ended the day unbeaten on 37 after a successful first day in his second spell as captain

Root was there at the end alongside Jordan Cox, making his first appearance at No 3

Root opted for Ollie Robinson’s ability to extract sideways movement over Jofra Archer’s extra pace or Gus Atkinson’s hustling accuracy and was vindicated when, from the first ball of the match from the Kirkstall Lane end, Pakistan’s rookie left-handed opener Azan Awais was trapped leg before.

There could not have been a better start to Root’s 66th match in charge than Chris Gaffaney raising his finger and the smiles and laughter continued unabated until Root responded to a huge jagging delivery from the fifth delivery of the over by shifting himself to second gully for the sixth.

Not that he stayed there for long. Some captains like to orchestrate things from the slip cordon: Root’s predecessors Andrew Strauss and Alastair Cook, England’s incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming and Australian great Mark Taylor amongst them.

Root also did this in the past, but having vacated first slip, and given up the job of chief ball-polisher in a bid to improve communication with his bowlers, standing on their shoulders at mid-off as Stokes had done during a four-year tenure, his stay was short-lived.

And in contrast to his captaincy performance as Stokes’ stand-in amid the midsummer chaos at the Oval when he unsuccessfully attempted to emulate some of his great friend’s funkiness, here he played the waiting game.

The trade-off for abandoning the close-catching cordon alongside Jamie Smith was a diminished perspective on DRS decisions and, duped by the enthusiasm of his team-mates, two reviews were wasted in the 50 minutes possible before rain stopped play: Imam-ul-Haq surviving a leg before claim by Robinson and one of caught behind off Atkinson that clipped pad rather than bat.

Root blew two of England's reviews in the first 10 overs, failing to have an LBW and caught behind call overturned

Those moments aside, Root was calm personified, rotating each of his four seamers and their ends.

He also took decisive action following a couple of flattering maidens by Jofra Archer from the football stand end of the ground, introducing Atkinson up the hill as early as the sixth over.

Root undoubtedly struggles to get the best out of Archer, as Stokes did, and the dynamic of their renewed relationship will remain under scrutiny this series. Changing ends did not improve Archer’s radar.

Root spent the second over of Archer’s second spell at third slip, maintaining an attacking field in the knowledge that catches here are commonly taken behind the wicket.

One challenge for Root will be getting the best from bowler Jofra Archer

Both in the pre-match huddle and during drinks, Root emphasised the need for fielders to take their chances here given that spells of sunshine coincide with run gluts.

Root also conversed with his vice captain Harry Brook during that second break in play, the hand gestures between them suggesting anticipation of a nick ending a disciplined stand of 91 between Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique.

Within half an hour it came to pass: Brook clasping a fine low catch at second slip to reward Root’s patience.

Only once Pakistan had lost half their team did he get creative with the field, posting two men on the drive either side of the wicket, as Robinson bowled straight with wicketkeeper Smith up to the stumps. When Josh Tongue found himself on a hat-trick, in came two short legs.

This was a day for traditional Test tactics, of line and length, of waiting for opponents to step out of sync - and Root, on this occasion, didn’t miss a beat.

Sports.title: Brighton's gifts from the Arctic Circle: Lewis Dunk and Co reward 407 hardy fans travelling for Euro clash in Tromso with free tickets and merchandise
Sports.content:
Brighton's gifts from the Arctic Circle: Lewis Dunk and Co reward 407 hardy fans travelling for Euro clash in Tromso with free tickets and merchandise

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brighton’s players have paid for tickets, T-shirts and scarves for more than 400 supporters who have travelled into the Arctic Circle to see them play against Tromso.

Captain Lewis Dunk explained why the players wanted to thank loyal fans ahead of the first leg of the Conference League play-off in Norway on Thursday.

'The fans didn’t know where they were going to go until the last minute,' said Dunk.

'It’s a long trip and last-minute to organise so we as a group of players wanted to make a gesture by refunding their tickets and give them a little present.

'Hopefully they appreciate it and it’s the start of a good season and we all enjoy it along the way.'

Brighton are back in Europe for their second campaign. They reached the last 16 of the Europa League in 2023-24 losing to Roma after winning a group featuring Ajax, Marseille and AEK Athens.

Lewis Dunk and Co rewarded Brighton fans by refunding their tickets for the Tromso clash

They have sold 407 tickets for the first leg at Tromso, who beat Cluj of Romania last week to set up the tie with Brighton.

'We’re not coming here and thinking it’s going to be easy,' said Dunk. 'It’s two games for a season’s work and we want to qualify for this competition.

'It’s the first game of the season. We’ve had a great pre-season and we’re raring to go.

'We’re an established Premier League side, finished high up in the table a lot of the time.

'We’d back ourselves against anyone in this competition. Let’s hope it goes well, we take a result back home and finish the job next week.'

Sports.title: Championship club Sheffield United at risk of 12-point deduction - with owners' company hit by winding-up order - as EFL investigate damaging breaches of rules
Sports.content:
Sheffield United are in danger of a 12-point deduction after the company its owners used to buy the club was hit with a winding up order.

Blades fans will now face an anxious wait while the EFL investigates whether there has been a potentially damaging breach of its rules.

United World, the investment arm of former owner Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, took COH Sports Bidco to the High Court, claiming it was owed £35million from the sale, which took place in 2024.

It argued that current custodians of the Championship side, American duo Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen, had effectively attempted to take the club without paying for it, after they transferred their shares in United to a new company.

While the Americans dismissed the move as a ‘publicity stunt’, a judge issued the winding up order and the EFL will now decide whether to take further action.

Sheffield United fans face a nervous wait to see if they are handed a 12-point deduction

A United World spokesman said it had ‘made every effort to resolve the matter amicably’ and had tried to do so again this morning ‘to give the owners a final opportunity to spare Sheffield United the consequences of their actions’.

‘It appears that Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are simply not concerned about what this means for the club,’ it added.

‘What happens now is the result of their choices. United World will continue to pursue the full sums.’

A Sheffield United spokesman said: 'Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner.

'The Football Club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected.'

Meanwhile, an EFL spokesman said: ‘The EFL notes the High Court’s decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited. The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required.

‘In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the club’s ownership structure and developments within the wider group. As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage.’

Sports.title: Man United summer target Ederson breaks silence over failed move to Old Trafford - revealing he passed medical so 'doesn't know what happened'
Sports.content:
Man United summer target Ederson breaks silence over failed move to Old Trafford - revealing he passed medical so 'doesn't know what happened'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Atalanta midfielder Ederson has attempted to shed some light on why his move to Man United collapsed earlier this summer.

Ederson, 27, was set to join the Red Devils for £39million as part of their midfield rebuild.

However, in early July, United pulled the plug on the transfer after it emerged that the 27-year-old’s initial medical had revealed a knee problem.

And Ederson, who subsequently signed a new contract with Atalanta, has admitted he is still confused as to why the deal didn't go through.

'I honestly don’t know what happened,' he said ahead of Atalanta's Conference League play-off clash against Hapoel Tel Aviv on Thursday.

'I always had interest from other clubs, and I could’ve gone to another English side.

Ederson has attempted to shed some light on why his move to Man United collapsed

The Atalanta midfielder was set to join United until the Red Devils pulled the plug on the move

'The tests went well, I don’t know what changed. I’ve been with Atalanta for four years and always played.

'I could’ve just waited to see what happened, but the great rapport with the club convinced me to stay and sign a new contract.'

At the time, United insiders insisted that it was the club’s intention to complete the transfer in early July after the structure of the deal and personal terms were agreed with Atalanta and the player.

However, Ederson received a late call-up for Brazil’s World Cup squad from coach Carlo Ancelotti after Roma defender Wesley was injured, forcing United to conduct the first part of the medical in the US.

After the knee problem emerged and a full medical was scheduled with the input of specialists after Brazil's exit from the tournament, United decided not to go through with the deal on the agreed terms.

Sources, who expressed sympathy for the player and his family, categorically denied United called it off before the full medical.

However, there was enough uncertainty for United to start making progress on other potential targets.

United instead made a move for Youri Tielemans, and also signed Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50m.

They are similarly hoping to add Brighton's Carlos Baleba before the end of the transfer window.

Ederson has made 180 appearances for Atalanta over the past four seasons, with the midfielder featuring 41 times in all competitions in 2025-26.

United backed out after the midfielder’s initial medical in the US revealed a knee problem

Despite the setback, the 27-year-old appeared to be at peace and outlined his excitement for the coming campaign.

He added: 'I had lovely moments going to the World Cup with Brazil, and then… I still don’t know what happened to be honest.

'But the important thing is that I was able to deal with the situation, return with the right mentality and give my all to the club that gave me so much.

'I am still Ederson, everyone knows me here and what I can do, they know I will always give my all.'

Ederson continued: 'I am very happy to remain with Atalanta, I really thank the club and (CEO) Luca Percassi.

'They called me many times, I felt they were by my side, but even though I had interest from other clubs, after everything that happened, I thought it was best to stick with who really wanted me, and that was always Atalanta.

'I was happy to wear the jersey that has given me so much joy.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
